messages:
sam: Hey team — PR 8140 is ready. Drops quant fallback CPU path and adds a fallback warmup knob. Bench data in CI: https://ci.internal/redwood/8140/bench. Can someone sanity-check p95 and throughput for longseq 8k and 32k? cc @jen @rafa
jen: taking a look now. quick Q: is the benchmark using the same batcher config as canary?
sam: yes, same batcher: `batch_size=16, max_latency_ms=20`. command we ran:
```
bench --model redwood-7b-q4f --seq 8192 --batch 16 --iters 200
```
rafa: opening artifacts. p95 for 8k looks +2.8% on canary vs main, throughput +3.1%. mem looks slightly lower. attaching snippet: `p95: 122ms -> 125ms, tps: 285 -> 294, rss: 6.1G -> 5.9G`
jen: hmm small p95 bump. can we get kv-cache warmup disabled? that knob `--kv-warmup=off` made it stable before?
sam: tried `--kv-warmup=off`, p95 back to 120ms, throughput 290. I left a note in the PR about fallback path being more aggressive which adds single-token jitter on tails.
infra-bot: canary run completed: canary-2029-03-12/8140: all checks passed. tail latency regression detected at p99+ but within alert threshold. link: https://ci.internal/canary/8140
kai: quick approval from me if jen ok with fallback knob defaulting to off for canary. we should gate default to off for major models.
jen: agree. small perf bump unacceptable for default. LGTM with `kv-warmup` default=off. @sam pls update PR description and add a feature flag.
sam: done — PR updated, feature flag `quant_fallback_kv_warmup=false` added. pinging for merge window today 16:00 PST.
rafa: I'll do the second approve after canary finishes full tail-run (~30m). If canary tail p99 stays within 5% we're good.
jen: re-approving now :thumbsup: 
sam: thanks! also logged a follow-up ticket to instrument single-token jitter in the runtime: #9271
rafa: noted. moving to merge queue for 16:00 PST slot.
sam: thanks team. If any weirdness during deploy ping me here.
